newsitem.title: GERMANY: Space officials urge U.N. action on space junk.
newsitem.headline: Space officials urge U.N. action on space junk.

text.p: Leading space officials on Wednesday urged the United Nations to create an international treaty to stop the explosive growth of space debris that threatens to turn the heavens into a junkyard.

The growing number of defunct satellites and other clutter in space will keep multiplying in the coming years, raising the risk of collisions unless action is taken soon, officials who attended a European Space Agency conference said.

"Space legislation is in critical need of a supplement for the issue of space debris since current laws are viewed as being too general," said Bess Reijnen, a professor of aerospace law at the Technical University of Deltf in the Netherlands.
"These legal issues should be dealt with by the United Nations as soon as possible," she added.
